_comment: Hanzi Dojo Stories — 'The Inkbound', episode 1. The canonical source for the manga episode: the Chinese, the line-parallel English, and the panel layout. publish-manga.mjs upserts this into `stories` (content / english_content / panels / presentation='manga'); src/mangaEpisodes.test.js validates the Chinese against the HSK 1 snapshot and the layout against the reader's own rules. Edit here, never in the database.
title: 第一话 · 我是新学生
english_summary: You climb the lantern-lit steps to the Hanzi Dojo and meet 小雨, who wants to know exactly one thing: are you the new student? Something small and white is watching from behind a lantern.
_content_comment: One beat per line, 'NAME：text' with a fullwidth colon, exactly as every other authored format stores it — the shared engine (useStoryReaderCore) tokenizes this and the manga reader only decides where each line is drawn. Beat indices are 0-based and are what panels[].bubbles[].beat refers to; INSERTING A LINE MEANS RE-INDEXING THE PANELS.
content:
我来学校了。
这是学校吗？
小雨：你好！你是新学生吗？
你：是，我是新学生。
你：不是！
小雨：真的吗？
小雨：我叫小雨。你叫什么名字？
林老师：我是林老师。
小雨：来吧！
小白也来了。
english_content:
I've come to the school.
Is this the school?
Hello! Are you the new student?
Yes, I'm the new student.
I'm not!
Really?
I'm called Xiao Yu. What's your name?
I am Teacher Lin.
Come on!
Xiao Bai came too.
_vocabulary_comment: Every word in this episode is HSK 1 (data/hsk1-vocab-snapshot.json). There are no reach words at all. The only tokens outside the word list are the three proper names, which are curated in src/characterNames.js so the reader gives them the 'Name' popup with a reading instead of translating them character by character. 小白 rather than the canon's 白: the reader's name matcher only takes names of two characters or more (matchName), so a one-character name would be read as the ordinary word 白 'white' — and 小白 is what you would actually call him.

meta.hook: Something small and white followed you through the gate. 第二话 is being drawn.

panels._cast_comment: A cast entry with a `display` gets a printed speaker label above its bubble; without one the bubble is bare, which is how a manga panel works — the drawing says who is talking. The speaker is still announced to screen readers either way.

panels.alt: Dusk. A young traveller with a scroll on their back stands small at the foot of a long stone stair, looking up at a lantern-hung dojo gate above a misty village.
Low angle: the huge tiled dojo gateway towers over the traveller, who is a small dark shape at the bottom of the frame.
Close-up: 小雨 leans grinning into the left of the frame, an ink brush through her hair and a red ribbon at one side; the right half of the panel is quiet empty wash.
小雨 in a lantern-lit courtyard, one hand at her chest as she introduces herself; the traveller's shoulder is in dark foreground at the left edge.
A letterbox panel: a tall calligraphy master stands in a doorway, face half in shadow, a brush held loosely at his side.
Almost darkness. A tiny white ink spirit with a single black brushstroke on its forehead peers out from behind a paper lantern, trailing a thread of ink-smoke.
The traveller walks in through the dojo gate, seen from behind; far back down the steps the small white spirit drifts after them.
